messages:
Maya Chen: OK team — SteadyFlow bring-up for AcmeCorp is scheduled Thu 2026-04-02 09:00 PT. Need final signoffs on quota, autoscale window, and the load script. TL;DR: target sustained QPS=1200, burst=3000, KV cache warmup ~30m.
Samir Patel: Copy, Maya. I'm double-checking the committed quota numbers from the contract. I think it's 1.2k steady, 3k burst, but want ops to confirm pool size. Link to workbook: https://redwood-internal/worksheets/acme/bringup (private)
Jordan Lee: From SRE side we need autoscale rules and cooldowns nailed. Proposal: min=2 nodes, max=18 (to cover 3k burst), cpu target 60% for scale decisions. Suggest 5m scale cooldown to avoid oscillation.
Maya Chen: @Jordan can you paste the short snippet we'll push to the autoscaler config?
Jordan Lee: Sure — small snippet for the playbook:
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 18
  cpu_target: 60
  scale_up_threshold: 80
  scale_down_threshold: 40
  cooldown_seconds: 300
```
Jordan Lee: We'll run a dry-run in staging with the same config.
Eli Torres: Runtime notes: model sharding + KV cache behavior means cold-start tokens spike for first 20m unless we prime. I'll run priming tasks 30m prior. Command I use: `./prime_kv.sh --pool acme --minutes 30 --parallel 8` — that warms prefix caches and populates KV across shards.
Samir Patel: Nice. For the load script I'll use the steady-ramp profile: 0→1.2k over 10m, hold 40m, spike to 3k for 5m, then cool down. File: `load_profiles/steadyflow-acme.yaml` — attaching to the runbook.
Nina Gomez: From CS/customer side: customer support hours are 08:00–18:00 PT — can we ensure the main cutover and heavy spike are inside that window? They want an earlier canary for 1 hour before full ramp.
Maya Chen: Yes — plan is: 08:00 PT canary (5% traffic), 08:30 PT ramp to 20%, 09:00 PT full steadyflow. Canaries will hit the dedicated pool only.
Jordan Lee: Canary health checks we'll monitor: 95th latency < 250ms, error rate < 0.1% for 5m window. If either triggers, autoscaler stays but traffic fallback to hosted.
Samir Patel: I added a quick rollback play in the runbook: if errors > 0.5% for 3m, run `./traffic-shift --to hosted --reason "acme bringup rollback"` and page oncall.
ops-bot: deploy-notify: Dedicated pool `acme-dedicated-v1` will be reserved 2026-04-02T07:30Z, priming jobs start at 07:30Z, canary at 15:00Z (09:00 PT).
Eli Torres: One more runtime caveat — quantized model variant has slightly different memory profile; if we hit OOM during priming switch to variant `acme-v1-light` via the runtime toggle: `redwoodctl variant set acme-dedicated acme-v1-light`. We'll log that in the incident channel.
Maya Chen: Checklist for tomorrow (short):
- [ ] Contract quota verified (Samir)
- [ ] Autoscale config validated & staging dry-run (Jordan)
- [ ] KV priming script run 30m before canary (Eli)
- [ ] Load script uploaded and smoke-tested in staging (Samir)
- [ ] Customer oncall present for canary (Nina)
- [ ] Rollback play bookmarked (Maya)
Samir Patel: I'll confirm contract numbers by EOD today and upload the final `steadyflow-acme.yaml`.
Nina Gomez: We'll have two customer engineers on-call for canary + ramp. I'll post their Slack handles in the morning.
Jordan Lee: I'll kick off the staging dry-run at 03:00 PT and post logs here. Expect a short noise window.
Maya Chen: Perfect. If no objections I'll mark this as ready and run the preflight checklist tomorrow 06:00 PT. :thumbsup:
